name: Crawford Commons
headline: A 60-home, all income-restricted townhome-style family rental community on county-donated land in unincorporated Clifton, sponsored by Housing Resources of Western Colorado with Evergreen Real Estate Group; it won 2026 Round One federal 9% and state credits.
why_it_matters: It is Clifton's first 9% award in about 25 years, built on land Mesa County donated, with a capital stack the sponsor calls fully committed: credits, a $2.4 million Prop 123 gap loan, a state grant, Capital Magnet Fund money and CHFA debt.

status.label: Credits awarded; construction expected spring 2027
status.detail: CHFA lists the award as of 2026-09-30. September 2026 news reports say construction should start in spring 2027 after final financing approvals and finish in fall 2028; no closing or permit record was found.

next_step: Watch for the Mesa County site plan review and building permit, and for the financing closing ahead of a spring 2027 start.

key_numbers.meaning: 16 at 30% AMI, 14 at 60%, 14 at 70% and 16 at 80% AMI; 20 one-bedroom, 20 two-bedroom, 10 three-bedroom and 10 four-bedroom.
About $18 million over 10 years (inferred), plus $500,000 in state credit.
Inferred from the application's total development cost of just under $408,739 per home; construction about $285,000 per home.
Given to the sponsor expressly for affordable housing, per CHFA and the application.

facts.value: 32 1/2 Road and Friendship Drive, Clifton (unincorporated Mesa County)
New construction; individual/family, with 20 units given a preference for older adults (intergenerational)
60 townhome-style rentals in six detached buildings, plus a separate community building with community room, flex space and management office
Zoned for multifamily (RMF-8 per the 2023 charrette); building permit expected 90-120 days after submission to Mesa County
2023 charrette describes a 12-acre site next to the sponsor's Jay Lee Apartments, with 5.5 acres for stormwater and 6.5 acres for housing
Next to a Grand Valley Transit Route 10 stop; about half a mile from the new Clifton Community Campus

money.source: Colorado standard state housing tax credit
Prop 123 Concessionary Debt (Affordable Housing Financing Fund, OEDIT/CHFA)
money.note: LIHTC gap loan for this project, selected 2026-07-21 (Round Two); $2,400,000 requested and awarded. Final terms set in underwriting.

money.source: Colorado Division of Housing, Housing Development Grant
money.note: Listed by the Division of Housing among its November 2025 rental awards (amount as requested; these appear to be conditional pre-application awards), and named in the application.

money.note: Mesa County donated the land to the sponsor; the 2023 charrette budget showed $0 acquisition cost.

background.text: Mesa County originally donated the land to Housing Resources of Western Colorado for affordable housing; no county resolution or deed record was found online.
The sponsor, a nonprofit founded in 1977, owns and manages 181 affordable rental units in five properties, including the neighbouring Jay Lee Apartments in Clifton.
Per the application, it will be the first LIHTC development in Clifton in 22 years and the first 9% project in 25 years; CHFA says the first in more than 20 years.

Design started at a three-day design charrette in October 2023 (Housing Colorado Now, with University of Colorado Denver and Kephart). That concept used 8-plex apartments and 4-plex townhomes for 60-90 homes for households under 60% AMI, with a $26.7 million budget including $12.3 million in 9% equity and $2.8 million in Division of Housing grant. The awarded plan now serves 30%-80% AMI in six townhome buildings.
Approvals: the site is already zoned for multifamily; the remaining public step is Mesa County formal site plan review. No county hearing or approval record was found.

Market study cited in the application: 5.4% capture rate; nearby Grand Valley Apartments (50 units) is full with more than 200 households waiting, and the Grand Junction Housing Authority waitlist is about 1,600 families.
Resident services: on-site workshops and counselling on renting, financial fitness and homebuying, from the sponsor.

Supporters listed in the application include the Mesa County Board of Commissioners, City of Grand Junction, Grand Junction Housing Authority and Clifton community leaders; the application reports no significant opposition.

discrepancies.text: The 2023 charrette lists a site address of 513 Jaylee Street, Grand Junction 81504, while CHFA lists 32 1/2 Road and Friendship Drive, Clifton.

open_questions: The CHFA loan amounts, equity price, rents and final total development cost are not public.
No Mesa County land donation resolution, site plan file or permit was found online.
Who will own and manage the finished property is not stated publicly.
Affordability period and any vouchers are not stated in public sources found.

The Division of Housing grant ($2,000,000) is listed by DOH as a November 2025 rental award at the requested amount; the final grant agreement is not public. The Capital Magnet Fund commitment ($1,500,000) was checked only against the application.
